newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: CRH says H1 profits will be lower than '96.
newsitem.headline: CRH says H1 profits will be lower than '96.

text.p: Irish building materials group CRH Plc said on Wednesday that the year had begun positively in all operating regions but group profits for the half year would be slightly lower than in the first half of 1996.
This reflected the higher financing costs of 1996 acquisitions and the seasonal North American trading pattern, CRH chairman Tony Barry told the annual meeting.
But Barry said that with a good start across all regions and a favourable full-year outlook, the group looked forward to a further year of growth in 1997.
Barry said growth in construction activity in Ireland had exceeded CRH's earlier expectations with particularly strong demand from the residential, commercial and industrial sectors.

Trading in Britain in recent weeks provided stronger evidence of improving demand in the company's product areas while CRH's operations in the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg got off to a strong start with more normal winter conditions than in 1996.
"Markets in Germany and France remain difficult while in Spain price weakness persists despite stronger demand," Barry said.

The group's North American operations are experiencing generally favourable trading conditions and the integration of the major 1996 acquisitions, Parson, Allied and Tilcon, has proceeded according to plan.

But CRH said first half trading profits for the enlarged North American group would be somewhat lower than in 1996 because the profitability of these acquisitions, particularly Tilcon, is significantly skewed toward the second half of the year.
"This reflects the tough winters prevailing in their main markets from which these businesses profit through repair and remediation," Barry said.
He said CRH had made good progress on the sale of surplus Tilcon assets with over $30 million of the planned $50 million of disposals already achieved.
The group, which reported pre-tax profits of 193 million Irish pounds in 1996, acquired Tilcon from BTR for $329 million last year.
